questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What is a principal advantage of offline retrieval evaluation?
options: It captures the parts of user value that behavioral metrics cannot express
It is repeatable and compares configurations without exposing users to them
It is free of judgment bias, since the labels are fixed before the comparison
It removes the need for production monitoring once the golden set is broad

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What does random assignment in an online A/B test primarily support?
options: A guarantee that users in both variants will behave in much the same way
A complete set of relevance judgments for the queries that were observed
A correction for the logging differences between the two experiment arms
A causal comparison between the eligible treatment and control traffic

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: Why can click-through rate misrepresent relevance?
options: Clicks can only be counted in offline replay, so live rankings are never covered
Every click marks a failed attempt, since a satisfied user leaves without clicking
Position and presentation attract clicks independently of a result's usefulness
A long dwell after a click proves the clicked result answered the user's need

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What should be checked before interpreting an online metric lift?
options: Assignment integrity, exposure, event schemas, sample ratios, and missing data
The treatment's mean query length measured against the control's at each decile
That offline nDCG on the same golden set has reached its maximum possible value
That every user in both arms clicked at least one result during the test window

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: Offline nDCG rises after long manuals are promoted, but task completion falls. What is a likely diagnosis?
options: Online randomization inverts true effects whenever dwell time is used as a guardrail
The labels reward authority more than the concise resolution users actually need
nDCG cannot score ranked lists in which the document lengths vary substantially
The manuals entered the index after the golden set's judgments had been collected

questions.topic: Offline vs Online Evaluation: When Each Lies
questions.question: What is the best response when offline and online results disagree?
options: Treat the click metrics as authoritative and retire the offline judgments
Ship whichever variant carries the newer retrieval model into production
Combine the offline and online numbers into one weighted decision score
Investigate labels, latency, presentation, logging, and the metric mechanisms

questions.question: Why is a system comparison across the same queries paired?
options: Each query yields one outcome per system, so the difference is measured within it
Both systems must return exactly the same documents before a comparison becomes valid
Each query carries an identical metric value once the labels are held fixed
Both systems must share a code path so that their scores stay commensurable

questions.question: What does a confidence interval around the mean paired delta communicate?
options: The probability that each relevance label in the set was assigned correctly
The business value the ranking change will deliver once it reaches real users
Uncertainty in the estimated average change under the resampling assumptions
The number of configurations that were compared before this one was chosen

questions.question: System A scores [0.4,0.7] and B scores [0.5,0.6]. What are the paired B minus A deltas?
Why should practical significance be assessed in addition to a p-value?
options: A p-value already reports how large the effect on the chosen metric was
Practical significance removes the sampling uncertainty from the estimate
Only effects that fail the significance test can be practically important
A clearly detected effect can still be far too small to matter operationally

questions.question: Why can testing 100 configurations and reporting only the smallest p-value be misleading?
options: Each extra configuration shrinks the paired sample available to the next test
Reporting a p-value hides the effect size, which is the only admissible evidence
Many comparisons make an extreme result likely even when nothing has changed
Paired differences cannot be formed once more than two systems are compared

questions.question: Many evaluation queries are near-duplicates from the same sessions. Which resampling choice is most defensible?
options: Resample individual queries and treat each near-duplicate as independent
Resample whole sessions or intent clusters rather than individual queries
Drop the treatment's scores and resample only the control arm on its own
Resample the relevance labels instead, holding the query sample itself fixed

questions.question: What is the main purpose of query-class error analysis?
options: To replace aggregate metrics with a narrative built from a few chosen cases
To confirm that every class in the taxonomy improved by the same amount
To remove the queries on which the treatment performs worse than control
To find repeated, actionable mechanisms behind gains and regressions

questions.question: Which pair describes two different useful kinds of class label?
options: Query intent and the failure mechanism suspected behind the result
The metric's mean and the confidence level chosen for its interval
The control ranking's depth and the treatment ranking's cutoff value
A document's byte size and the position it held before reranking

questions.question: What evidence should accompany a mean metric delta for a query class?
options: One representative winning query, quoted with its full ranked result list
Query count, baseline level, uncertainty, win rate, and severe regressions
The size of the index and the number of distinct terms in its vocabulary
The share of the class's documents that the reranker managed to reorder

questions.question: Why should newly discovered post-hoc classes be treated as hypotheses?
options: Because a class defined after the run cannot be applied to any future query
Because only online experiments allow results to be sliced into segments
Because repeated slicing can manufacture convincing patterns purely by chance
Because post-hoc classes always inherit the label errors of the golden set

questions.question: A relevant document is absent from the final top k. What is the best first diagnostic sequence?
options: Check corpus presence, indexing, candidate sources, fusion, rerank, and filters
Raise the fusion weight on every candidate source until the document finally appears
Assume the judgment is stale and relabel the document as irrelevant instead
Widen the metric cutoff until the document falls inside the evaluated depth

questions.question: A hybrid ranker improves broad queries but harms exact error codes because semantic candidates crowd out lexical matches. What is a targeted remedy?
options: Remove the exact-match index so both candidate sources score the same way
Restrict the evaluation to broad natural-language queries and re-run the test
Reserve slots for exact-match candidates or make the fusion query-dependent
Grade every semantic candidate as irrelevant so that fusion demotes them all
